lines.line: node bin/csv2json.js --tsv reads tab-separated input on stdin and prints a JSON array with one object per row, keyed by the header row
lines.evidence: Wrong build: bin/csv2json.js changed to `parse(input, '\t')` unconditionally (or `parse(input, /[\t,]/)` regardless of flag), with no test added. `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints [{"a":"1","b":"2"}], so this line passes. But plain `node bin/csv2json.js < table.csv` no longer splits on commas (or with the regex, splits CSV fields that contain tabs, and splits TSV fields that contain commas). The existing test/csv.test.js 'cli' test would catch the unconditional-tab version, but no expect line says `npm test` must pass or that CSV with no flag must keep working. Nothing requires a regression test for --tsv either: a PR with no test meets every line, and later edits can break --tsv silently. Missing lines: (a) running node bin/csv2json.js without --tsv on comma input gives the same output as before (or `npm test` passes, existing tests unchanged); (b) test/ has a test that runs the CLI with --tsv on tab input and checks the JSON output. The proof's `printf ...` also leaves the input unspecified. One reader could check a single row and another a multi-row input with an empty trailing field, and they could grade the same PR differently.

Tried a README that only mentions the word, e.g. 'see also --tsv'. A reader of README.md checking whether it 'documents --tsv' would expect a usage line like `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`, in the style of the existing usage block, and would see that a bare mention doesn't document anything. The repo has one short README with a single usage block, so this check is easy to make and two careful readers should agree. I found no wrong build that meets this line on its own and misses the request's documentation need.

result.wrong_build: A PR that changes bin/csv2json.js to call parse(input, '\t') whenever process.argv includes --tsv, and also to split on /[\t,]/ by default "to be lenient". It adds a --tsv usage line to README.md and adds no test. `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints [{"a":"1","b":"2"}] and the README documents --tsv, so both expect lines pass. But default CSV parsing has changed: comma input whose fields contain tabs now gets split wrongly. No regression test guards --tsv, and nothing requires the existing CSV behaviour or `npm test` to stay green. A simpler variant always splits on tab and breaks CSV entirely; only the existing test, which no line requires anyone to run, would catch it.
